title: Finite-Step Sinkhorn Certificates for Nonnegative Stream-Mixing Products

AI.tldr: The paper derives deterministic finite-step bounds on the induced norms of products of nonnegative stream-mixing matrices in expanded-stream residual architectures, using Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections as the motivating case.
AI.motivation: Forward and backward gain control of the mixer pathway in deep expanded-stream residual networks needs certificates that hold for finite depth and finite Sinkhorn steps, not only asymptotically.
AI.method: Row and column marginal defects of nonnegative mixers are shown to control induced norms; a column-then-row Sinkhorn order gives a product bound min{prod(1+eps_c^(l)), n}, complemented by a telescoping refinement, a depth-uniform Dobrushin certificate under uniform scrambling, and a Hilbert-projective argument that converts logit range, temperature and a Sinkhorn step cap into a backward budget.
AI.result: Numerical diagnostics on marginal defects, realized and certified gains, finite-step calibration, cap failures and normalization cost in matched and stress-test settings; the abstract gives an asymptotic rate of sigma_2(P)^2 from matrix-specific local analysis.
AI.conclusion: The certificates cover only the mixer pathway; full-network stability also depends on the nonlinear residual branches, so the bounds are necessary-scope limited but give concrete finite-depth control of mixer gains.

title: From Text to Voice: A Reproducible and Verifiable Framework for Evaluating Tool Calling LLM Agents

AI.tldr: The paper converts verified text tool-calling benchmarks into audio evaluations with text-to-speech, speaker variation and environmental noise, and evaluates 7 omni-modal models on Confetti and When2Call.
AI.motivation: Voice agents need reliable speech-based tool use, but prominent tool-calling benchmarks are text-only and re-annotating them for audio is costly.
AI.method: A dataset-agnostic pipeline builds paired text and audio instances while preserving the original tool schemas and gold labels, adds text-only results, an ambiguity-based reformulation stress test, and a reference-free LLM-as-judge protocol validated against human preferences.
AI.result: Gemini-3.1-Flash-Live scores highest on Confetti (70.4) and GPT-Realtime-1.5 highest on When2Call (71.9); the text-to-voice gap on Confetti ranges from 1.8 points (Qwen3-Omni) to 4.8 points (GPT-Realtime-1.5); open-source Qwen3 judges with at least 8B parameters reach about 80% agreement with proprietary judges.
AI.conclusion: Performance is strongly model- and task-dependent, failures mostly reflect misunderstood argument values in speech, and the pipeline is offered as a verifiable, reproducible first-stage diagnostic that complements purpose-built audio corpora.

title: Reproducing "The Tug of War Within: Mitigating the Fairness-Privacy Conflicts in Large Language Models"

AI.tldr: This reproduction study checks the SPIN method of Qian et al. (2025), which suppresses fairness-privacy coupled neurons in LLMs, across three instruction-tuned models and extends it to new settings.
AI.motivation: Fairness and privacy improvements in LLMs often trade off against each other, and the original SPIN claims to resolve this without training; the claim needed independent verification.
AI.method: The authors re-run the original evaluation on three instruction-tuned LLMs, then extend it with more data-scarce conditions, a new neuron localization method, and tests on the safety-helpfulness trade-off.
AI.result: SPIN generally improves both fairness and privacy while preserving general capabilities and remaining effective under malicious and limited-data settings, consistent with the original paper; transfer to the safety-helpfulness trade-off is mixed across models.
AI.conclusion: SPIN's effectiveness holds under various conditions, but its transfer to other alignment trade-offs is inconsistent, suggesting coupled-neuron behaviour is context-dependent.

title: Is the Geometry Doing the Work? An Operating-Point Audit of Hierarchy in Hyperbolic Vision–Language Models

AI.tldr: An audit of seven released and matched hyperbolic vision-language checkpoints (MERU, HyCoCLIP, PHyCLIP) finds that they operate near-Euclidean and do not show an operative hierarchy beyond angular structure.
AI.motivation: Hyperbolic vision-language models are assumed to encode abstraction geometrically through radius and entailment cones, but it was unclear whether trained models actually use these mechanisms.
AI.method: The authors use diagnostics on the dimensionless radius u = sqrt(c)*rho, entailment-cone saturation, preregistered semantic-traversal analysis, shuffle-controlled radial-ordering tests, and matched from-scratch interventions with curvature-floor release and gradient decomposition.
AI.result: The largest image-side u is 0.37, well below the 0.84 at which local metric distortion reaches 10%; cones are saturated or nearly saturated; no pair-specific radial ordering is detected; the diagnostic reaches 80% power only at about 13.5 pp excess while the largest released gap is about 5 pp.
AI.conclusion: A low-curvature shortcut widens cones and suppresses violations without learning order, so the audited formulations do not demonstrate an operative radial or cone-based hierarchy; the paper proposes a five-number geometry report for future hierarchy claims.

title: PID-DiffRL: Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning as Noisy Delayed Feedback Control

AI.tldr: PID-DiffRL is a safe offline RL framework that replaces the integral-only Lagrange multiplier update with a PID update, uses max aggregation over twin cost critics, and uses diffusion policies.
AI.motivation: In offline safe RL the multiplier update relies on learned cost critics evaluated on out-of-distribution actions, so the feedback is biased, delayed and noisy.
AI.method: The method treats adaptive penalty learning as feedback control, with a proportional-integral-derivative multiplier update, max aggregation of twin cost critics to counter optimistic cost underestimation, and diffusion policies to represent multimodal safe action distributions.
AI.result: On DSRL benchmarks PID-DiffRL achieves strong reward-safety trade-offs, consistently reducing constraint violations to near zero while keeping competitive reward.
AI.conclusion: Treating the safety multiplier as a feedback-control problem, together with critic aggregation and expressive policies, is presented as an effective approach to offline safe RL.

title: PRIVET: PRoximIty leakage detection Via Extreme value Theory

AI.tldr: PRIVET is a sample-level, modality-agnostic leakage detector that uses extreme value statistics on nearest-neighbour distances to give each synthetic sample a continuous proximity leak score.
AI.motivation: Existing proximity-based privacy assessments are global and cannot attribute risk to individual records, while existing sample-level outputs are uncalibrated, discontinuous, or blind to leakage in underfit models.
AI.method: Each synthetic sample is scored by how improbable its nearest-neighbour proximity to the training set is under a no-leakage model, evaluated under a chosen representation and distance.
AI.result: PRIVET detects memorization and subtler proximity leakage across diverse modalities, including high-dimensional genetic data with small sample sizes and underfitting regimes that overfitting-based diagnostics cannot reach; the authors also show that existing computer vision embeddings fail to give perceptually meaningful distances for near-duplicates.
AI.conclusion: A low score is evidence of leakage in the chosen metric, but a high score is not a certificate of privacy, and the representation bounds what any distance-based evaluation can detect; an open-source implementation is provided.

title: SOMA: Structured and Orthogonal Matrix Adaptation for Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning of Transformers

AI.tldr: SOMA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that extends VeRA by using structured orthogonal transforms for the low-rank update and placing the low-rank bottleneck on the trainable diagonal matrices instead of the frozen random projections.
AI.motivation: VeRA's frozen random matrices have an uncontrolled singular value spectrum, which can make updates poorly conditioned and hurt fine-tuning performance.
AI.method: The low-rank update is formulated with structured orthogonal transforms while keeping VeRA's update form, and a low-rank constraint is imposed on the learnable diagonal matrices so that conditioning depends mainly on these trainable factors.
AI.result: On VTAB-1k and common-sense reasoning benchmarks, SOMA achieves competitive accuracy with fewer trainable parameters than existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Controlling conditioning through the trainable diagonal factors gives an efficient alternative to VeRA-style adaptation, though the abstract reports only competitiveness rather than clear gains.

title: Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the standard before-and-after-cutoff check for contamination in LLM backtests is uninformative, and proposes known-cutoff and matched-clean-control estimators that yield leakage-adjusted scores.
AI.motivation: Models know more about periods near their training cutoff, so recency alone mimics leakage, and passive backtests cannot separate leakage from genuine skill.
AI.method: The authors prove that no passive backtest can separate the two, then supply external information through a known cutoff to localize leakage at the boundary and a matched clean control to estimate it globally, modelling leakage under a convex-pull assumption.
AI.result: Four flagship models fail the naive check on questions they cannot have memorized; in twin models with planted leakage the estimators detect, localize and dose-track leakage and return null on clean questions; on frontier models they find no significant leakage at the tested boundaries in five models with positive naive gaps.
AI.conclusion: Backtests need not be discarded, but they need a defensible reference such as a known cutoff or matched control before results are interpreted as skill.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Function Space Regularization

AI.tldr: FedFun is a decentralized federated learning framework that enforces client consensus in function space as a proximal regularization penalty in a Hilbert space of hypotheses.
AI.motivation: Parameter-space consensus assumes shared architectures and well-behaved objectives, which excludes heterogeneous clients and non-parametric learners.
AI.method: Agreement between neighbouring clients is written as a regularization penalty in a Hilbert space of hypotheses and optimized with proximal gradient updates, supporting both parametric and non-parametric learners.
AI.result: The authors provide convergence guarantees under modest assumptions, including non-convex client objectives, and give proof-of-concept experiments on tabular data with neural networks and decision trees, including a case where model type differs across clients.
AI.conclusion: Function-space consensus allows decentralized training across differing architectures with convergence guarantees, though the empirical evidence is limited to proof-of-concept tabular experiments.

title: Reference-Guided Machine Unlearning

AI.tldr: ReGUn is a vision unlearning method that distills forget-set predictions toward a class-conditioned reference distribution built from disjoint held-out data, instead of degrading predictions on forget samples.
AI.motivation: Degradation-based unlearning heuristics such as loss maximization or random labeling are poorly conditioned, destabilize optimization and harm generalization, while the goal is for forget data to behave as unseen data.
AI.method: The approach uses disjoint held-out data to construct a class-conditioned reference distribution and distills it into the model, aligning forget-sample predictions with those on truly unseen data.
AI.result: Across multiple architectures, natural image datasets and forget fractions, ReGUn consistently improves the forgetting-utility trade-off over standard approximate baselines and closely matches retrain-like membership inference behaviour.
AI.conclusion: Objectives built on distributional indistinguishability can be an effective and simpler alternative to degradation-based unlearning.

title: Scaling Laws: A Model-Based Optimization Perspective

AI.tldr: This position paper maps neural scaling laws onto the three stages of Model-Based Optimization (design space, surrogate modeling, guided optimization) and proposes a bi-level formulation over model, data and hyperparameter subspaces.
AI.motivation: Scaling-law practice is a special case of Model-Based Optimization, but the literature has focused on power-law priors and neglected the wider MBO perspective.
AI.method: The authors identify three characteristics that distinguish scaling from standard MBO (low-dimensional spaces, strong power-law priors and strict compute constraints), partition the design space into model, data and hyperparameter subspaces, formalize a bi-level problem with hyperparameters optimized at the lower level, and apply autofocus to surrogate extrapolation covariate shift as a proof of concept.
AI.result: The abstract reports only an illustrative proof-of-concept applying autofocus to mitigate extrapolation-induced covariate shift; no quantitative results are stated.
AI.conclusion: The paper proposes a research roadmap emphasizing uncertainty quantification and multi-objective optimization for scaling-law work.

title: Soft Probabilistic Discrete Minimax Classifier

AI.tldr: SPDMC is a deterministic, profile-based classifier that iteratively updates class priors to balance empirical class-conditional risks, with bisection in the binary case and a heuristic projected update in the multiclass case.
AI.motivation: Class imbalance or prior shift can produce large disparities among class-conditional risks, especially in non-separable settings where the global risk depends strongly on the priors.
AI.method: Soft probabilistic discrete Bayesian classification is combined with profile-based posterior approximation and an iterative risk-driven prior update; under zero cost for correct predictions, equal empirical class-conditional risks imply empirical minimax optimality within the classifier family.
AI.result: Experiments on imbalanced binary and multiclass datasets show SPDMC generally achieves better class-conditional risk balance than resampling, class-weighted logistic regression and class-weighted decision tree baselines; the multiclass update reduces risk imbalance but has no convergence guarantee.
AI.conclusion: Prior optimization offers an interpretable, efficient route to risk-balanced classification with proven empirical minimax properties in the binary case and heuristic guarantees in the multiclass case.

title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback via Advantage Sign Robustness

AI.tldr: SignCert-PO mitigates reward hacking in RLHF by down-weighting policy-gradient updates on completions whose advantage sign is not robust to adversarial perturbation of the reward model parameters.
AI.motivation: Reward hacking is attributed to flipped advantage signs, where an update meant to reduce a bad response's likelihood increases it; prior fixes need multiple reward models or access to RM training data.
AI.method: The authors derive a certified sign-preservation radius, the smallest RM parameter perturbation that flips the advantage sign, and use it to down-weight non-robust completions during policy optimization, using only RM parameters and on-policy completions.
AI.result: On TL;DR summarization and AlpacaFarm, SignCert-PO achieves a better win rate than baselines in most cases and reduces reward hacking.
AI.conclusion: The method is a lightweight, purely policy-stage defence against reward hacking, with gains reported in most but not all settings.

title: DS-RNNs: Conditional Computation in Recurrent Models via Input-Dependent Sparse Gating

AI.tldr: DS-RNNs apply learned, input-dependent sparse gating to recurrent models and state-space models so that each input runs a sparse subnetwork whose size is fixed by a target sparsity budget.
AI.motivation: Recurrent and state-space models run the same dense computation for every input, which couples inference cost to parameter count and causes interference in multi-task settings; prior methods such as DeltaRNNs and RigL are either not fully learned or static.
AI.method: A small router predicts sparse masks over input and hidden-state channels, with structured masking that reduces sparse matrix multiplications to dense operations on active submatrices; a theoretical bound links the behaviour to gradient interference.
AI.result: DS-RNNs keep most dense performance at 90% sparsity across LSTMs, GRUs, LTCs and S4 models, match or outperform RigL and DeltaRNNs on most tasks, induce class-specific subnetwork specialization, and reduce forgetting when combined with GEM or replay.
AI.conclusion: Input-dependent structured sparsity gives budget-controlled conditional computation with practical FLOP savings and better robustness in multi-task and continual learning, according to the authors.

title: Toward Fair Speech Technologies: A Comprehensive Survey of Bias and Fairness in Speech AI

AI.tldr: This survey reviews bias and fairness in speech AI across more than 400 studies, formalizing seven speech-adapted fairness definitions and linking them to evaluation, diagnosis and mitigation.
AI.motivation: Fairness work in speech is fragmented across tasks and disciplines, and existing surveys either take a general ML view that ignores speech-specific properties or cover only one task.
AI.method: The survey organizes the field into three paradigms (Robustness, Representation, Governance), maps evaluation metrics into six families tied to the definitions they operationalize, diagnoses bias sources along the speech pipeline, and systematizes mitigation across four intervention stages.
AI.result: The abstract names speech-specific mechanisms such as channel bias as a demographic proxy and annotation subjectivity in emotion labels, but reports no quantitative results since it is a survey.
AI.conclusion: The survey offers a unified framework for speech fairness research and identifies open challenges and future directions.

title: Understanding Robust Overfitting in Adversarial Training of GNNs:A Stability and Generalization Perspective

AI.tldr: The paper analyses robust overfitting in adversarial training of GNNs and derives a generalization bound of O(1/n) by smoothing the adversarial loss with Moreau Envelope techniques, improving on the earlier O(1/n + xi) bound.
AI.motivation: Adversarial training of GNNs suffers from robust overfitting due to the non-smooth adversarial objective, and the earlier bound showed a penalty from perturbation strength xi that needed mitigation.
AI.method: The authors introduce smoothness approximation techniques for the adversarial loss, analyse the stability of the resulting training, and extend the study to black-box zeroth-order attacks, examining GCN, APPNP and GCNII with architecture choices and weight-norm regularization.
AI.result: The bound improves to O(1/n) with the Moreau Envelope, zeroth-order optimization degrades significantly compared with first-order methods, and suitable architecture factors and weight-norm regularization improve robust generalization.
AI.conclusion: Smoothing the adversarial loss, especially with the Moreau Envelope, theoretically and empirically helps robust generalization of GNNs, while zeroth-order black-box settings remain harder.

title: Revisiting Class-Incremental Learning in the Era of Foundation Models: A Gaussian Density Estimation Perspective

AI.tldr: The paper treats class-incremental learning on frozen foundation-model embeddings as recursive estimation of class-conditional Gaussian densities, using mixtures of up to four Gaussians with full or shared covariance.
AI.motivation: Once representations are frozen and discriminative, the core CIL problem becomes modelling class distributions rather than protecting parameters from forgetting, which existing regularization, replay and architectural methods do not exploit directly.
AI.method: The approach fits Mixture-of-up-to-four-Gaussians models (MOG4-F with full covariance and MOG4-Shared with shared covariance) recursively, validates per-feature Gaussianity with D'Agostino-Pearson and Diagonal Henze-Zirkler tests, and measures inter-class separability with the Bhattacharyya distance.
AI.result: The method achieves competitive performance on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R and Caltech-256 with significantly lower computational cost than the compared methods, according to the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Density estimation on frozen foundation embeddings is a simple, principled and cheap alternative for class-incremental learning with a probabilistic interpretation.

title: Toward More Robust Quantile Conformal Hyperparameter Optimization

AI.tldr: The paper audits and extends conformalized quantile regression for hyperparameter optimization (CQHPO), establishing conformal guarantees and benchmarking adaptive and non-adaptive intervals across surrogates, acquisition functions and design parameters.
AI.motivation: Prior work gave limited evidence that conformal calibration helps or stays valid under sequential sampling and explored only a narrow range of surrogates, acquisition functions and parameters.
AI.method: The authors state conformal guarantees, benchmark adaptive and non-adaptive conformal intervals, add linear and ensemble estimators to the surrogate set, propose a discretized approximation of Expected Improvement, and run sensitivity analyses on design parameters and failure modes.
AI.result: Conformalization benefit depends strongly on the acquisition function; some architecture and acquisition combinations beat existing CQHPO front-runners on key benchmarks; in external comparisons CQHPO underperforms Gaussian Processes on generic benchmarks and trails or matches SMAC on categorical ones.
AI.conclusion: Conformal calibration in CQHPO is useful only for certain acquisition-surrogate combinations and its overall standing against GPs and SMAC is mixed.

title: Controlling Foundation Models via Internal Interventions: A Survey of Inference-Time Methods

AI.tldr: This survey reviews inference-time internal interventions on foundation models, categorizing methods into representation-level, attention-level and decoding-level interventions across LLMs, VLMs and diffusion models.
AI.motivation: Inference-time interventions offer reversible, request-time control without changing parameters or prompts, but the methods differ in preparation, access requirements and side effects, and no unified structured review existed.
AI.method: The survey uses a structured narrative review with explicit literature-selection criteria, classifies methods by the computational component they modify, gives a formal treatment of the transformer as a computational graph, and discusses linear steering from empirical and theoretical perspectives.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative results since it is a survey; it analyses interventions across three model classes and compares the work with existing surveys.
AI.conclusion: The paper discusses strengths and limitations of the techniques and outlines future directions for steering foundation models.

title: MoE$^2$-LoRA: When MoE Models meet MoE-style Low-Rank Adaptation

AI.tldr: MoE2-LoRA applies MoE-style low-rank adaptation to Mixture-of-Experts models, coupling pretrained router activations with LoRA routing and sharing one global LoRA expert pool across layers.
AI.motivation: Existing PEFT methods for MoE models either ignore router priors with uniform adapters or use static expert selection, which limits per-token capacity and cross-expert feature learning.
AI.method: A dual-channel Routing-Conditioned Projection module reuses base router activations to inform LoRA routing, and a single global LoRA expert pool is shared across all layers to enable model-wide adaptation with balanced expert utilization.
AI.result: MoE2-LoRA achieves the strongest downstream performance among the evaluated methods across multiple MoE backbones while preserving general capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Combining prior reuse, dynamic adapter routing and model-wide sharing is presented as an effective PEFT strategy for MoE models; code is released.

title: Naïve Difficulty Conditioning Fails on ShapeNet-55: A Matched-Control Audit

AI.tldr: The paper shows that apparent double-digit gains of a naive difficulty-conditioned extension of AdaPoinTr on ShapeNet-55 are artefacts of warm-start mismatch, and that under a matched control the extension underperforms.
AI.motivation: Earlier reported per-bin CD-l2 gains for the DiffCond extension were compared with a from-scratch baseline, so the evaluation needed a matched-control check and a disciplined protocol.
AI.method: The authors propose a stratified matched-control protocol that pins warm-start, schedule, crop path and pre-specified decision thresholds, report results at four evidence tiers, apply it to DiffCond, run a static audit and a three-seed ablation, and add a cross-backbone replication on UpTrans and a 2-seed PCN sanity check.
AI.result: Under the matched control DiffCond shows a 5.48% Hard and 4.56% Mean CD-l2 regression across three seeds, missing the acceptance threshold on every bin; a Hard-Specialist probe gives an exploratory +7.38% with a 95% CI crossing zero; on UpTrans no cell clears the +3% bar, with the largest paired mean at +1.79%.
AI.conclusion: The best-supported claim is bounded: this specific naive extension underperforms its matched control on ShapeNet-55, shows no large gain on UpTrans, and warm-start mismatch explains the original apparent gain.

title: Looking beyond the next token

AI.tldr: Trelawney is a data-only method that interleaves training sequences with special lookahead tokens carrying future information, letting an autoregressive model condition on and generate future goals without architectural changes.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive training assumes each token is predicted from prior context only, which mismatches non-linear, hierarchical human writing and reasoning, and prior work assumed architectural changes were needed.
AI.method: Training data is augmented by interleaving sequences with special lookahead tokens that contain future information, requiring no change to architecture or training infrastructure.
AI.result: Representative results on path planning, algorithmic reasoning, zebra puzzles and controllable generation show improved performance on tasks with branching paths or long-horizon planning, and the model can generate plausible long-term goals.
AI.conclusion: Rearranging and augmenting the training data alone can move autoregressive modeling closer to the true data-generating process, which the authors suggest may open capabilities beyond the current paradigm.

title: Exploring Extrinsic and Intrinsic Properties for Effective Reasoning with Code Interpreter

AI.tldr: The paper characterizes what makes reasoning with a code interpreter effective, examining crucial tokens and code-specific cognitive behaviours, and tests using them at inference and training time.
AI.motivation: Code-interpreter reasoning is widely adopted, but the behavioural properties behind effective code reasoning are underexplored.
AI.method: Across multiple LLMs the authors measure the prevalence of crucial tokens (extrinsic) and cognitive behaviours such as verification, backtracking and backward chaining (intrinsic); they append code-specific crucial tokens at inference and augment a state-of-the-art framework with code-specific cognitive behaviours for SFT and RL training.
AI.result: Stronger CI reasoning models show more crucial tokens and cognitive behaviours; appending crucial tokens improves mathematical, ordering and optimization reasoning with limited gains elsewhere; the added behaviours improve SFT and RL in two of three evaluated models and reduce overthinking in incorrect responses.
AI.conclusion: Key properties can be leveraged to improve code-interpreter reasoning, but gains are model-dependent and the paper gives the first systematic characterization of this reasoning mode.

title: NSFL: A Post-Training Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic Framework for Boolean Operators in Neural Embeddings

AI.tldr: NSFL is a training-free framework that adds fuzzy-logical Boolean operators to dense neural embeddings, anchoring logic on atomic similarity scores and steering with contextual Neuro-Symbolic Deltas.
AI.motivation: Standard dense retrievers have no native mechanism for multi-atom logical constraints, and geometric baselines suffer from representation collapse and manifold escape.
AI.method: Logical operations are anchored on zero-order atomic scores and corrected by first-order finite-difference Neuro-Symbolic Deltas; for latency-constrained use, Spherical Query Optimization uses Riemannian optimization to project logical formulas into manifold-stable query vectors.
AI.result: Across six encoder configurations and two modalities, NSFL raises mAP@100 by up to +81% on QUEST and +70% on a COCO-derived text-to-image benchmark, adds about +19% on average to an encoder already fine-tuned for logical retrieval, and doubles NevIR pairwise accuracy from 0.256 to 0.508.
AI.conclusion: The decomposition is presented as exact and general, while the operators are engineering realizations rather than a closed algebra, a boundary the authors state explicitly.

title: Towards Generalist Game Agents: A Survey of Foundation Models in Virtual Worlds

AI.tldr: This survey traces foundation-model generalist game agents across four eras and four pillars (Dataset, Model, Harness, Benchmark), and proposes a five-step roadmap toward agents that create and evolve game worlds.
AI.motivation: Games are a proposed ground for training and evaluating AGI, but progress is scattered across symbolic, reinforcement learning and foundation-model work with no end-to-end view.
AI.method: The authors trace the lifecycle of a generalist game player along four pillars and frame each advance as an attempt to break one of five fundamental trade-offs bounding the system, then chart a five-step roadmap.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative results since it is a survey.
AI.conclusion: The survey offers a unified lens on the field and a roadmap from single-game mastery to a creator stage in which agents build and evolve game multiverses.

title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents

AI.tldr: This survey defines execution provenance and evidence tracing for LLM agents, giving a six-dimensional taxonomy and nine provenance relations, and finds gaps in fine-grained provenance, end-to-end benchmarks and tamper-evident traces.
AI.motivation: Final-answer evaluation cannot show which evidence supported claims, whether tool calls were justified, how memory shaped decisions or where failures began, and related work on attribution, tool safety, memory and observability is fragmented.
AI.method: The survey frames agent runs as typed provenance graphs, projects them to evidence-support relations, builds a six-dimensional taxonomy, defines nine provenance relations and two attributes (provenance origin and trace assurance), and applies the framework to the surveyed systems and benchmarks.
AI.result: Three gaps are identified: limited integration of fine-grained provenance with multiple trust functions, no benchmark in the catalog evaluating the complete provenance chain, and little reporting of tamper-evident or attested traces.
AI.conclusion: Final-answer correctness alone cannot establish process-level trust, motivating unified trace schemas, provenance-aware safety, realistic benchmarks and privacy-aware auditing; the authors maintain a resource list.

title: Retrieval-Free Instruction Selection for Instruction-Tuned Embedding Models via Uncentered Spectral Entropy

AI.tldr: IPP ranks instruction candidates for instruction-tuned embedding models without retrieval evaluation or labels, by scoring each instruction with the normalized spectral entropy of the second-moment matrix of its proxy query embeddings.
AI.motivation: Choosing a query instruction normally requires retrieval evaluation with corpus access and judged queries, which is unavailable in cold-start domains, API-only services and large candidate pools.
AI.method: For each candidate instruction the method embeds a small unlabeled set of query-like proxy texts and scores the normalized spectral entropy of the second-moment matrix, as a retrieval-free and label-free screen.
AI.result: Across 16 embedding models, 17 retrieval datasets and all 272 model-dataset pairs, IPP reaches median oriented Spearman rho = 0.806 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.710, 0.871]) and median regret@1 of 0.004 NDCG@10 points on a 104-instruction pool.
AI.conclusion: The score predicts instruction quality, with the mechanism left open, and the method should hand off to direct retrieval evaluation when candidate instructions produce little downstream variation.

title: Demasking Fine-Tuning for Knowledge Injection in Autoregressive and Diffusion LLMs

AI.tldr: The paper shows that training with a demasking objective, reconstructing text from a masked copy given in context, lets autoregressive LLMs learn knowledge from raw text without paraphrase augmentation and mitigates the reversal curse.
AI.motivation: Fine-tuning autoregressive LLMs on plain knowledge text generalizes to QA only with paraphrase augmentation and suffers from the reversal curse, whereas masked diffusion LLMs appear not to need paraphrases.
AI.method: Controlled knowledge fine-tuning experiments compare masked diffusion LLMs with autoregressive LLMs, and the autoregressive models are then trained with an added demasking objective in which the model reconstructs the original text from a masked copy.
AI.result: Adding the demasking objective to autoregressive models improves knowledge injection, removes the need for paraphrases, mitigates the reversal curse and recovers most of the gap to diffusion LLMs; preliminary evidence suggests it helps on a large-scale knowledge-intensive dataset.
AI.conclusion: The bidirectional demasking objective is a practical way to improve knowledge injection in autoregressive LLMs, with broader applicability still preliminary.

title: UniDoc: Towards Unified Thinking in Documents

AI.tldr: UniDoc answers questions over long, visually rich documents with a two-stage, resolution-adaptive pipeline: low-resolution Fast Reading to find evidence pages, then high-resolution Focused Thinking on those pages only.
AI.motivation: Retrieval-augmented methods fragment documents and lose inter-page structure, while monolithic vision-language models scale poorly beyond a few pages.
AI.method: A single model decouples perceptual resolution across stages, and it is trained on 30K multi-hop reasoning instances with stage-level supervision.
AI.result: On MMLongBench-Doc, UniDoc gives relative accuracy gains of 55.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 16.9% on Qwen3-VL-8B while significantly reducing token cost relative to uniform high-resolution processing; page retrieval and fine-grained visual reasoning remain the main bottlenecks.
AI.conclusion: Adapting resolution per stage combines structural holism with the efficiency of targeted retrieval for long documents, and the authors identify concrete targets for future work.

title: The Zero-Shot Illusion in the Wild: Diagnosing Boundary Failures in AIGC Detection

AI.tldr: WildGen is an in-the-wild benchmark showing that AI-generated image detectors which look strong on curated benchmarks fail on real-world AI images, and that few-shot source-level adaptation restores detection performance.
AI.motivation: Many detectors report strong zero-shot results on curated benchmarks but generalize poorly to real-world images produced by multi-model workflows with LoRAs, adapters and post-processing, a gap the authors call the zero-shot illusion.
AI.method: The authors build WildGen from 342K community-created AI images across 342 sources and 347K real images from 8 datasets, evaluate training-based and training-free detectors, probe frozen CLIP features with linear heads, and test few-shot source-level adaptation and joint fine-tuning with GenImage and ForenSynths.
AI.result: 11 of 12 training-based methods stay below 58% balanced accuracy and the best training-free method reaches 75.21% AUC; few-shot adaptation reaches 97.20% mean balanced accuracy across five runs (95.69% with 18 examples per source).
AI.conclusion: Detectors should be reported with their valid distributional boundary, and few-shot updates serve as a practical maintenance tool as generators evolve.

title: Estimating Rare Events in Language Models with Proper Evaluation

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Shifted-Power Bregman (SPB) loss, a proper scoring rule that stays finite for zero estimates, and GA-AMLS, a gradient-based activation-space rare-event estimator for language models. It finds that the best estimator depends on the asymmetry of the deployment cost.
AI.motivation: Estimating the probability of rare failures in language models is fragile: standard evaluation losses become unstable or mismatched to asymmetric safety costs, and estimators suffer zero-estimate collapse or systematic bias. Prior activation-space estimators rely on independence assumptions.
AI.method: The SPB loss is a proper scoring rule that remains finite at zero estimates and has a tunable asymmetry between underestimation and overestimation penalties. GA-AMLS adapts adaptive multilevel splitting to the continuous activation space, using a gradient-based MCMC kernel and conditional sampling under an explicit, heavier-tailed activation prior.
AI.result: Experiments on small transformer models show distinct bias and cross-token dispersion profiles. GA-AMLS often outperforms the strongest baseline under symmetric evaluation, while methods with overestimation bias perform best under asymmetric penalties and have lower cross-token dispersion. GA-AMLS reduces zero-estimate failures of input-space search.
AI.conclusion: Estimator choice should be matched to the deployment context, and activation space is a tractable domain for rare-event estimation in language models that avoids the brittleness of discrete input-space search.

title: On Designing Diffusion Autoencoders for Efficient Generation and Representation Learning

AI.tldr: The paper argues that diffusion autoencoders (DAs) have unrealised potential as generative models and proposes DMZ (diffusion models with z), a DA variant whose design choices for latent variables and conditioning improve generation and representation learning.
AI.motivation: DAs use an input-dependent latent variable for representation tasks, but its effect on unconditional generation depends strongly on how the variable is modelled, learnt and used in denoising, and this generative potential has not been realised.
AI.method: The paper connects DAs to diffusion models that learn their own forward (noising) process, and develops DMZ by choosing the latent variables and the conditioning method deliberately.
AI.result: Across extensive experiments and ablations, DMZ converges in fewer iterations, generates high-quality samples with fewer denoising steps, and learns effective latent representations for downstream classification and domain transfer.
AI.conclusion: Careful design of the latent variable and conditioning makes DAs competitive generative models without losing their representation-learning ability, showing that DAs have been under-exploited as generators.

title: STRIDE: Continual Learning using Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding

AI.tldr: STRIDE is a continual-learning framework for physics-based character controllers that encodes reusable behavioural primitives as discrete codewords with a VQ-VAE, so new skills are learned by combining existing codewords. It accelerates downstream learning by 1.3x to 2.0x over baseline frameworks while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
AI.motivation: Reinforcement-learning controllers for general-purpose physics-based characters suffer policy interference in continuous spaces. Training isolated controllers avoids interference but costs significant training overhead and produces disjointed transitions between behaviours.
AI.method: Policy quantization via a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) dynamically discovers and encodes reusable behavioural primitives in a discrete latent space. New behaviours and tasks are learned by combining existing codewords, which act as a stable motion prior that structurally eliminates catastrophic forgetting.
AI.result: Evaluated on diverse locomotion styles, agile manoeuvres such as kicking, and composite tasks such as target-aiming, STRIDE accelerates downstream learning by 1.3x to 2.0x compared with baseline learning frameworks. The discrete representations also allow direct tracking of skill activations and behavioural decisions during task execution.
AI.conclusion: STRIDE offers a scalable and transparent approach to continual character control that improves interpretability without compromising motion quality.

title: Obey, refrain, or contravene: disobedience as a basis for responsible autonomy

AI.tldr: The paper develops a conceptual model of intelligent disobedience for agents in human-agent teams, extending prior work on refraining from execution to disobedience by contravention, meaning the execution of an alternative course of action. It shows that the manner of disobedience affects when disobedience is appropriate.
AI.motivation: Agents sometimes ought to disobey human commands because of the commander's situational misunderstandings, changing conditions, cognitive biases, miscommunication or incomplete information. Prior work on disobedience focuses only on inaction (refraining from execution) and does not consider disobedience by contravention.
AI.method: The authors create a conceptual model of intelligent disobedience that covers both refraining from execution and contravention, and they run simulations of this model.
AI.result: Simulation results from the model show that how an agent disobeys determines when it is appropriate for that agent to disobey.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the implications of intelligent disobedience for collaborative settings and suggest that responsible autonomy must consider the form of disobedience as well as whether to disobey.

title: Heuristics and models in approval voting: Results from a real-world study

AI.tldr: The paper studies how people vote in single-winner and multi-winner approval voting under uncertainty, using Mechanical Turk behavioural data. It finds that people manipulate their ballots but rarely find the optimal manipulation, and proposes a model that outperforms existing heuristic models in multi-winner settings.
AI.motivation: Agents may manipulate approval ballots to obtain better outcomes, but computing the best manipulation is effortful in complex and uncertain situations, so they use heuristics. Existing predictive models of agent behaviour from social choice and psychology, which rest on cognitively plausible heuristics, do not adequately model real-world data.
AI.method: Behavioural data were collected from Mechanical Turk for single-winner and multi-winner approval voting under varying degrees of uncertainty. The authors propose a novel model that considers the size of the winning set and human cognitive constraints.
AI.result: People generally manipulate their votes to obtain a better outcome, but often do not identify the optimal manipulation. Existing approaches do not adequately model the data, whereas the proposed model captures real-world behaviour more effectively in multi-winner approval voting.
AI.conclusion: Modelling human voting in approval elections needs to account for the size of the winning set and cognitive constraints, not only the heuristic strategies previously proposed.

title: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks

AI.tldr: DMAST co-trains multimodal web agents and attackers to resist cross-modal prompt injection. It nearly halves out-of-distribution attack success while improving task completion.
AI.motivation: Web agents using screenshots and accessibility trees can be simultaneously corrupted through DOM injection, and text-centric VLM safety training does not address visually assisted attacks.
AI.method: DMAST models agent-attacker interaction as a zero-sum Markov game and uses teacher imitation, oracle-guided SFT with zero acknowledgment, and GRPO self-play.
AI.result: On out-of-distribution tasks, attack success falls from 41.2% to 21.4% and task completion rises from 6.2% to 10.2%, outperforming training- and prompt-based defenses.
AI.conclusion: Co-evolutionary adversarial training can improve multimodal web-agent robustness and generalization to unseen environments.

title: Dementia-R1: Reinforced Pretraining and Reasoning from Unstructured Clinical Notes for Real-World Dementia Prognosis

AI.tldr: Dementia-R1 uses RL-based pretraining on clinical indices to predict dementia progression from longitudinal notes. It achieves leading results on real-world, Parkinson's disease, and ADNI cohorts.
AI.motivation: Dementia prognosis requires reasoning over non-monotonic symptoms across visits, but symptom-evolution labels are unavailable and direct RL has sparse rewards.
AI.method: Cold-Start RL first teaches prediction of verifiable indices extracted from patient histories, then supports final clinical-status reasoning.
AI.result: Dementia-R1 reaches 84.02% AUROC on a real-world cohort, 78.37% on an independent Parkinson's disease cohort, and 83.17% on ADNI with a 7B model.
AI.conclusion: Reinforced clinical-index pretraining enables effective longitudinal reasoning from unstructured notes for real-world prognosis.

title: Improving Diffusion Language Model Decoding through Joint Search in Generation Order and Token Space

AI.tldr: Order-Token Search jointly explores generation order and token values for diffusion language models. It improves mathematical reasoning and coding decoding performance to a level comparable with diffu-GRPO post-training.
AI.motivation: Existing DLM decoders commit to one generation trajectory despite the models' order-agnostic generation space.
AI.method: The method uses a likelihood estimator to score denoising actions, enabling stable pruning while searching diverse order-token trajectories.
AI.result: It improves backbone accuracy by 3.1%, 3.8%, 7.9%, and 6.8% on GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, and HumanEval, respectively.
AI.conclusion: Joint search over generation order and token space is an important decoding component for DLMs.

title: PsyAgent: Constructing Human-like Agents Based on Psychological Modeling and Contextual Interaction

AI.tldr: PsyAgent builds personality-grounded agents by combining Big Five trait profiles with structured social contexts. It improves trait faithfulness and multi-turn persona consistency under controlled evaluation.
AI.motivation: Human-like agents must remain dispositionally stable while adapting to roles, relationships, and norms.
AI.method: PsyAgent couples an Individual Structure trait profile with Multi-Scenario Contexting frames, and can synthesize IS times MSC supervision for PEFT through SFT and optional DPO.
AI.result: It improves trait-faithfulness and persona consistency, is competitive with larger instruction-tuned baselines, and is supported by external benchmarks and a small blinded human study.
AI.conclusion: Explicit trait-context schemas offer a precise, data-efficient route to norm-aware personality agents.

title: Forget What’s Sensitive, Remember What Matters: Token-Level Differential Privacy in Memory Sculpting for Continual Learning

AI.tldr: PeCL adds token-level differential privacy and privacy-guided memory sculpting to continual learning. It protects sensitive information while preserving task-invariant knowledge and prior-task accuracy.
AI.motivation: Uniform DP budgets protect all accumulated continual-learning data equally, causing excessive utility loss in privacy-sensitive settings.
AI.method: PeCL allocates DP budgets by token semantic sensitivity and uses that analysis to forget sensitive memory and parameters while retaining invariant historical knowledge.
AI.result: Experiments show a better privacy-utility balance than baselines, maintaining high accuracy on prior tasks while providing robust privacy.
AI.conclusion: Sensitivity-aware privacy allocation and memory editing can make continual learning more private without indiscriminately eroding utility.

title: GR-SAP: Generative Replay for Safety Alignment Preservation during Fine-Tuning

AI.tldr: GR-SAP preserves LLM safety alignment during downstream fine-tuning by generating synthetic domain-specific alignment data. It reduces fine-tuning-induced safety degradation without sacrificing downstream performance.
AI.motivation: Mixing original alignment data into fine-tuning can preserve safety, but those data are usually inaccessible for open-weight models.
AI.method: GR-SAP applies generative replay to synthesize alignment data from LLMs and integrates it with downstream adaptation.
AI.result: Theoretical and empirical analyses support synthetic data as a proxy for original alignment data, and experiments across models and tasks show substantial safety preservation with comparable task performance.
AI.conclusion: Generative replay is a practical substitute for inaccessible alignment corpora during fine-tuning.

title: Demographic Prompting at Scale: When More Attributes Hurt LLM–Human Agreement

AI.tldr: This study finds that demographic prompting has highly task- and model-dependent effects on LLM-human agreement, and adding all attributes is never best. Small attribute subsets usually work best when prompting helps.
AI.motivation: It is unclear how the number and composition of annotator demographic cues affect agreement between LLM predictions and human labels.
AI.method: Five open-source LLMs are evaluated across five tasks under every combination from single demographic attributes to full profiles, with neuron probing analysis.
AI.result: Baseline prompts are best in 12 of 25 model-task pairs; in 11 of the other 13, 1-3 attributes are optimal, and full-attribute prompts are never optimal.
AI.conclusion: Demographic prompting is not a uniform intervention; useful cues require learnable, directionally coherent annotation signals.

title: ALEE: Any-Language Evaluation of Embeddings via English-Centric Minimal Pairs

AI.tldr: ALEE evaluates text embeddings in any language using English AMR-based minimal pairs and translations. Its study across 275+ languages exposes persistent cross-lingual semantic-representation gaps.
AI.motivation: Existing embedding benchmarks are static, narrow in language coverage, domain-specific, overfittable, and poorly representative of low-resource languages.
AI.method: ALEE extends Sentence Smith to cross-lingual paragraph evaluation by generating controlled English semantic shifts and pairing them with target-language translations.
AI.result: Across embedding models, 275+ languages, and three parallel datasets, performance varies substantially by language, length, and phenomenon, tracking training-resource prevalence and subword tokenization.
AI.conclusion: English parallel data can support broad, fine-grained diagnostics of multilingual embedding quality.

title: CoPRM: A Collaborative Process Reward Model for Guiding Search Agent Reasoning

AI.tldr: CoPRM is a process reward model for search agents trained from collaboratively calibrated preference data. It provides efficient, consistent gains across four multi-hop QA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Search-agent PRMs rely on unreliable single-source supervision that cannot jointly ensure global solvability and local validity.
AI.method: Collaborative Calibration combines immediate assessments with outcome-informed evaluations, using consensus filtering and outcome-informed gating to construct preference pairs.
AI.result: Trained on 10k preference pairs, CoPRM provides universal test-time guidance and improves diverse search agents across four multi-hop QA benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Combining complementary assessment signals can produce more reliable process supervision for search-agent reasoning.

title: TTSR: Test-Time Self-Evolving via Reflection

AI.tldr: TTSR lets one model alternate between Student and Teacher roles to improve itself at test time through reflection. It delivers consistent gains on hard math reasoning and transfers across backbones and general reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: Test-time training suffers from noisy pseudo-labels on hard questions and inefficient rollout sampling without diagnosing prior failures.
AI.method: The Student solves and updates while the Teacher analyzes failures and synthesizes targeted near-frontier variants; a weakness memory becomes a lightweight strategy note for later attempts.
AI.result: Experiments on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks show consistent test-time improvement, cross-backbone generalization, and transfer to general-domain reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Reflection-guided sample synthesis and persistent weakness tracking can make unlabeled test-time adaptation more effective.

title: Gated Residual Discrepancy for Efficient Bi-Encoder Factuality Verification

AI.tldr: GRD is an efficient bi-encoder factuality verifier that models asymmetric entailment and filters contextual noise. It approaches the strongest cross-encoder's accuracy at much higher speed.
AI.motivation: Joint evidence-claim encoders are expensive, whereas efficient bi-encoders struggle with asymmetric entailment and noisy long contexts.
AI.method: GRD extracts dual-view vector differences in a difference-dominant design and uses adaptive gating to remove distracting contextual information.
AI.result: GRD obtains 79.99% average Macro-F1, only 1.15 points below the strongest cross-encoder, with a 23.55 times speedup and far fewer FLOPs.
AI.conclusion: Difference-focused, noise-gated bi-encoding enables sensitive factuality verification at substantially lower cost.

title: Entropic properties of languages in phonetic versus orthographic alphabets

AI.tldr: A study of 42 languages finds generally small Shannon-entropy differences between phonetic and orthographic representations. This convergence varies by language and representational granularity.
AI.motivation: Computational linguistics mainly uses writing, but whether written and spoken encodings share information-theoretic properties is unresolved.
AI.method: The authors compute continuous entropy trajectories over DoReCo data at word, BPE-subword, and character levels using orthographic and phonetic encodings.
AI.result: Orthographic and phonetic entropy is consistently close across levels overall, though examples such as English, Bora, and Sanzhi Dargwa show level-specific gaps.
AI.conclusion: Entropy appears broadly modality-invariant for the examined Latin-script languages, while typology may drive meaningful divergence.

title: Self-Calibrating Language Models via Test-Time Discriminative Distillation

AI.tldr: SECL self-calibrates LLM confidence through test-time discriminative distillation without correctness labels. It sharply reduces calibration error while adapting only under distribution shift.
AI.motivation: LLMs are overconfident, and existing calibration methods need labeled validation data, degrade under shifts, or add substantial inference cost.
AI.method: SECL uses the model's P(True) answer-correctness signal as self-supervision, adapting on shifted inputs with two hyperparameters set from a small labeled probe.
AI.result: Across five 2B-12B models and four domains, SECL reduces ECE by 56-78% while training on only 6-26% of questions and matching or exceeding recent inference-time methods.
AI.conclusion: Test-time distillation of latent discriminative confidence offers label-efficient, robust LLM calibration.

title: Escaping the Ambiguity Trap: Content-Level Evidence Tracing for Open-Domain Table QA

AI.tldr: PGR improves open-domain table QA by tracing content-level evidence within retrieved table segments before answering. It reaches strong evidence-localization and end-to-end accuracy on Open-WikiTable.
AI.motivation: Retrieval representations cannot reliably distinguish relevant evidence segments when retrieved table pieces share similar metadata and schemas.
AI.method: PGR generates query-specific metadata and cell-level probes to rerank segments, then applies a decoupled Semantic-Plan-Execute workflow optimized with GRPO.
AI.result: With fixed BM25 candidates on Open-WikiTable, PGR reaches 85.96% segment-level evidence accuracy at k=5 and 69.0% end-to-end QA accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Content-level evidence verification can ground downstream table reasoning more reliably than candidate retrieval alone.

title: Parallel Tokenizers: Rethinking Vocabulary Design in Cross-Lingual Transfer of Low-Resource Languages

AI.tldr: Parallel tokenizers align monolingually trained vocabularies across languages to share semantic representations. They outperform conventional multilingual tokenization baselines on four low-resource-language tasks.
AI.motivation: Conventional multilingual tokenizers assign semantically equivalent words in different languages to different vocabulary indices, limiting transfer especially for low-resource languages.
AI.method: The framework trains tokenizers per language then exhaustively aligns vocabulary items using bilingual dictionaries or word-to-word translation.
AI.result: Transformer encoders pretrained on 13 low-resource languages outperform conventional multilingual baselines on sentiment, hate speech, emotion classification, and sentence-similarity tasks.
AI.conclusion: Vocabulary alignment is a useful lever for improving cross-lingual representation learning in low-resource settings.

title: STARK: Strategic Advantage Reinforcement with Confidence-Driven Exploration for Long-Horizon Agentic Learning

AI.tldr: STARK improves long-horizon agent RL through confidence-guided branching and dual strategic-tactical advantage estimation. It outperforms strong baselines across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop.
AI.motivation: Linear parallel rollouts collapse to homogeneous reasoning patterns, while existing credit assignment cannot jointly compare states and discriminate meta-reasoning quality.
AI.method: STARK branches and reflects at uncertain keypoints, then estimates strategic advantages across reasoning modes under shared observations and tactical advantages within meta-reasoning groups.
AI.result: It consistently outperforms strong baselines across model scales and domains, with a 1.5B model surpassing GPT-5 on out-of-domain settings.
AI.conclusion: Confidence-driven exploratory branching plus dual-track credit assignment can strengthen long-horizon agent learning.

title: How Much Supervised Fine-Tuning Is Enough? Dissecting the Impact of SFT Extent on Downstream Reinforcement Learning Performance

AI.tldr: This work analyzes how the extent of supervised fine-tuning affects subsequent RL performance for LLMs. It aims to identify checkpoints balancing domain grounding with exploration capacity.
AI.motivation: SFT can narrow plausible-output exploration, whereas RL needs a sufficiently aligned initialization; practitioners lack guidance on when to transition between them.
AI.method: The study quantitatively examines SFT extent and downstream GRPO-style RL across multiple domains, focusing on exploration-exploitation behavior and final performance.
AI.result: The abstract reports a quantitative multi-domain analysis intended to guide selection of SFT checkpoints that maximize final performance while minimizing post-training overfitting.
AI.conclusion: SFT and RL should be treated as complementary stages whose balance determines downstream adaptation quality.

title: AuroraCounsel: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Collaboration Framework for Psychological Counseling

AI.tldr: AuroraCounsel is a multi-agent LLM counseling framework with emotion-driven routing and GRPO-aligned guidance. It improves professionalism, empathy, and interaction appropriateness in evaluator and counselor assessments.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM counseling systems struggle with complex emotion dynamics and theory-grounded pacing across counseling phases.
AI.method: The system combines emotion sensing, structured reflection, and guidance agents; it activates reflection for negative emotion and optimizes guidance behavior with GRPO.
AI.result: LLM-based evaluations and professional-counselor assessments show consistent improvements over existing approaches in professionalism, empathy, and appropriate interaction.
AI.conclusion: Emotion-aware routing and phase-sensitive RL alignment can better model professional counseling workflows.

title: Long Document Reconstruction Unlocks Scalable Long-Context RLVR

AI.tldr: This work uses RL to reconstruct missing paragraphs in long documents, creating verifiable supervision for long-context learning without human QA labels. It improves RULER and LongBench v2 performance.
AI.motivation: Long-context RLVR commonly requires costly gold answers or expert rubrics, limiting scalable training.
AI.method: The model identifies and orders paragraphs removed from documents and replaced with placeholders, learning global narrative coherence through reconstruction rewards.
AI.result: The method gains nearly 10 points on RULER and achieves a reasonable improvement on LongBench v2 without manually curated long-context QA data.
AI.conclusion: Long-document reconstruction provides scalable unsupervised verifiable rewards for improving long-context capabilities.

title: HIPO: Instruction Hierarchy via Constrained Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: HIPO frames hierarchical instruction following as constrained RL, explicitly enforcing system-prompt compliance while maximizing user utility. It improves both outcomes across Qwen, Phi, and Llama models.
AI.motivation: RLHF and DPO optimize largely single objectives, while SFT imitates compliant examples without establishing instruction-priority asymmetry.
AI.method: HIPO models instruction following as a constrained MDP and uses primal-dual safe RL to optimize user utility within a system-compliant feasible region.
AI.result: Evaluations across diverse architectures show improved system compliance and user utility; mechanistic analysis finds increased attention to long-range system tokens.
AI.conclusion: Treating system instructions as optimization constraints provides a principled basis for reliable hierarchical instruction following.

title: Audio-Reward-R1: Reasoning Reward Model for Unified Audio Understanding and Generation

AI.tldr: Audio-Reward-R1 is a reasoning reward model for audio understanding and generation preferences, supported by a reasoning-enhanced dataset and a human-verified benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal reward models are insufficiently interpretable and unreliable for audio-centric preference judgments.
AI.method: The model produces dimension-level reasoning before preference judgments, is cold-started with structured reasoning traces, then trained with RLVR; Audio-Reward-Bench evaluates both audio tasks.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of Audio-Reward-R1.
AI.conclusion: Structured reasoning supervision can make audio reward modeling more interpretable and reliable.

title: Beyond Junk Tokens: Subsumed Tokens in Japanese Subword Tokenization

AI.tldr: This work identifies subsumed tokens as valid Japanese words suppressed by longer overlapping tokens and proposes post-processing to restore them. It improves representation quality without harming downstream task performance.
AI.motivation: Frequency-based subword tokenization creates junk fragments and can suppress valid shorter words contained in longer tokens.
AI.method: The method searches binary character segmentations for frequency-maximizing tokenizations, optionally rewarding morphological-analyzer word spans, and can post-process BPE or ULM tokenizers.
AI.result: On Wiki-40B Japanese, it reduces overlapping tokens, yields more reliable word-frequency statistics, improves representation quality, and preserves downstream performance.
AI.conclusion: Post-processing existing vocabularies can mitigate overlapping-token artifacts without retraining tokenizers.

title: On the Optimality of Kinship Naming: an Information-theoretic Approach

AI.tldr: This work studies the informativeness-complexity trade-off in kinship naming across four languages and learned communication systems. It finds that trade-off optimality can emerge empirically.
AI.motivation: Earlier accounts of kinship naming assume universal communicative needs and optimal listeners, simplifying real linguistic variation.
AI.method: The authors collect four-language data, vary communicative needs and listener models, and use a referential-game setup from emergent communication.
AI.result: The analysis shows how communicative need and listener variation affect the trade-off, and learned communication systems empirically exhibit achievable optimality.
AI.conclusion: Kinship naming efficiency depends on language-specific communicative conditions and listener assumptions.

title: To Answer or to Abstain: Mitigating Search-Agent Hallucinations via Abstention-Aware Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: AWA-RL trains search agents to abstain when retrieval cannot support an answer, reducing hallucinations while retaining capability. It improves precision and the new capability-reliability metric RA-F1.
AI.motivation: Outcome-reward training rewards correct answers but does not penalize fabricated answers after failed retrieval, encouraging search-agent hallucination.
AI.method: AWA-RL dynamically shapes abstention rewards using query-specific prior capability and continuous on-policy observations, and evaluates the trade-off with RA-F1.
AI.result: Compared with non-abstaining baselines, it improves absolute precision by up to 10.3% and RA-F1 by 2.9%, with only marginal raw-accuracy loss.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive abstention rewards can make search agents more reliable without substantially sacrificing answer capability.

title: More Test-Time Compute Can Hurt: Overestimation Bias in LLM Beam Search

AI.tldr: This study shows that widening LLM search can hurt when candidate scoring is noisy, with useful width depending on scorer reliability. A PRM benefits from beam widening, whereas perplexity does not.
AI.motivation: Beam-width selection work emphasizes efficiency without asking whether wider search can reduce reasoning quality through noisy rankings.
AI.method: The authors analyze noisy candidate ranking with a Gaussian model and compare perplexity scoring with a PRM across three 7-8B models and ten MR-BEN subjects.
AI.result: Perplexity gains no accuracy at any tested width, while the PRM gains up to 8.9 points and improves through beam width 4 with 16 candidates per step; 444K steps support the ranking model.
AI.conclusion: More test-time search helps only when the scorer is sufficiently reliable relative to candidate quality gaps.

title: LDC: Learning to Generate Research Idea with Dynamic Control

AI.tldr: LDC generates research ideas with controllable SFT and RL that balance novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness. It dynamically navigates these competing dimensions during inference.
AI.motivation: Prompt-only research-idea generation often fails expert standards, and balancing novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness is difficult because they trade off.
AI.method: LDC learns paper-to-follow-up-idea patterns through SFT, optimizes multi-dimensional rewards during RL, and uses sentence-level dimensional controllers at inference.
AI.result: The framework reports high-quality research-idea outcomes by dynamically balancing novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: Controllable post-training can provide a balanced approach to automated scientific ideation.

title: When Denser Credit Is Not Enough: Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Training

AI.tldr: ECPO calibrates step-level RL credit for long-horizon LLM agents to prevent noisy, low-evidence advantages. It improves over GiGPO with negligible additional computation.
AI.motivation: Dense credit in group-based RL can overvalue rare lucky actions under limited rollouts, causing bias and unstable late-stage training.
AI.method: ECPO combines action-grouped, low-count-shrunk Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage with Variance-Gated Credit Weighting that suppresses noisy anchor states.
AI.result: On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, ECPO improves GiGPO by 5.2 and 7.3 success points for Qwen2.5-1.5B, adding only 0.1% advantage-computation overhead.
AI.conclusion: Calibrating credit by action evidence and noise can stabilize and improve critic-free long-horizon agent RL.

title: GeoMotionGPT: Geometry-Aligned Motion Understanding with Large Language Models

AI.tldr: GeoMotionGPT aligns motion-token and LLM embedding geometry through orthogonality constraints. It substantially improves motion understanding and motion-language reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing pipelines connect motion quantization and semantic embeddings only through token IDs, failing to align motion-space and embedding-space geometry.
AI.method: The framework uses a Gumbel-Softmax decoder-only quantizer, orthogonality-preserving sparse projection, and two-stage orthonormal regularization during tokenizer and LLM training.
AI.result: It improves aggregate Average by 22.4% over the strongest baseline on HumanML3D and 14.4% on KIT-ML; ablations validate each design.
AI.conclusion: Giving motion codes and language embeddings a shared geometric basis improves nuanced motion reasoning.

title: Response-Aware User Memory Selection for LLM Personalization

AI.tldr: RUMS selects LLM personalization memories using their mutual information with outputs rather than query similarity. It yields more human-aligned selections, better responses, and far lower cost.
AI.motivation: Similarity-based memory selection ignores how memory items actually change the model's response distribution.
AI.method: RUMS measures mutual information between a candidate memory subset and model outputs, favoring items that reduce response uncertainty and sharpen predictions.
AI.result: It aligns more closely with human selection than state-of-the-art methods and models 400 times larger, improves response quality, and reduces computation by up to 95%.
AI.conclusion: Response utility is a more principled and efficient criterion for choosing personalization memory.

title: Stabilizing Unsupervised Self-Evolution of MLLMs via Continuous Softened Retracing reSampling

AI.tldr: CSRS stabilizes unsupervised MLLM self-evolution with retracing, continuous frequency rewards, and visual semantic perturbation. It achieves state-of-the-art geometric-task results with Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
AI.motivation: Majority-vote pseudo-labels can reflect a model's biases rather than objectively correct reasoning, degrading self-evolution.
AI.method: CSRS retraces from anchor points to explore long-tail paths, replaces binary rewards with softened frequency rewards, and uses visual perturbations to prioritize mathematical logic.
AI.result: CSRS significantly improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B reasoning on MathVision and achieves SOTA results for unsupervised self-evolution on geometric tasks.
AI.conclusion: Diverse retracing and continuous reward calibration can stabilize unsupervised multimodal reasoning improvement.

title: RW-TTT: Batched Serving for Request-Owned Test-Time Training State

AI.tldr: RW-TTT enables correct batched serving for request-owned test-time-training state. It preserves per-request behavior while substantially increasing throughput.
AI.motivation: Request-specific updates such as fast weights break the shared static-weight assumption of batched serving; serial serving is slow and naive batching corrupts state.
AI.method: RW-TTT tags decoding steps by owner, version, and read/write effect, batches only compatible phases, and commits updates only to the corresponding owner.
AI.result: With eight fast-weight In-Place-TTT streams on one GPU, it reaches 274.61 aggregate tok/s, 9.31 times sequential speed and 3.44 times memory-matched replicas, while preserving RULER behavior.
AI.conclusion: Read-write scheduling makes stateful TTT compatible with efficient, correct batched LLM serving.

title: ParaBridge: Bridging Paralinguistic Perception and Dialogue Behavior in Speech Language Models

AI.tldr: ParaBridge teaches speech language models to turn paralinguistic perception into appropriate dialogue behavior without curated dialogue labels. It strongly improves safety and empathy-related dialogue measures while preserving general ability.
AI.motivation: SLMs recognize cues such as tone and background noise but often ignore them in open-ended dialogue; inference-time scaffolds are brittle.
AI.method: An on-policy self-distillation setup uses a temporary scaffolded privileged view to provide dense next-token targets along scaffold-free model rollouts.
AI.result: On Qwen3-Omni-thinking, VoxSafeBench SAR rises from 14.6% to 40.3% and EchoMind rating from 3.27 to 3.92, while MMAU-Pro, VoiceBench, and GPQA remain within 0.4 points.
AI.conclusion: Scaffold-derived self-distillation can make latent paralinguistic cues reliably influence spoken dialogue.

title: Ready to Speak: Aligning LLMs for TTS-Friendly Text Generation

AI.tldr: This work aligns LLMs to generate text that is naturally suitable for text-to-speech rather than rewriting it afterward. FaST achieves the best reported trade-off between TTS-friendliness and helpfulness.
AI.motivation: LLMs optimized for written text can produce grammatically sound responses that are awkward when spoken by TTS systems.
AI.method: The authors introduce CORA and Recipe preference datasets and evaluate alignment using heuristic patterns, TTS-to-ASR, and MUSHRA human listening; they compare FaST with alignment baselines.
AI.result: FaST performs best overall across settings, and the evaluation metrics correlate strongly, supporting efficient heuristic assessment of TTS-friendliness.
AI.conclusion: Direct preference alignment can make LLM output more speech-ready while preserving helpfulness.

title: From Accuracy to Robustness: A Study of Rule- and Model-based Verifiers in Mathematical Reasoning

AI.tldr: This study analyzes rule- and model-based mathematical verifiers in static evaluation and RL training. Rule-based verifiers miss equivalent answers, while model-based verifiers can be reward-hacked.
AI.motivation: Verifier reliability and its consequences for RLVR remain poorly understood despite their central role in training reasoning models.
AI.method: The authors compare multiple verifier types in static evaluation and reinforcement-learning settings for mathematical reasoning.
AI.result: Rule-based verifiers produce substantial false negatives that increasingly limit stronger policies; model-based verifiers improve static accuracy but misclassify exploitable response patterns after fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Both verifier families have distinct robustness failures, motivating more accurate and reward-hacking-resistant RL reward systems.

title: PGA-KD: Principal Geometry Alignment and Semantic Consistency for VLM2Vec Distillation

AI.tldr: PGA-KD distills VLM2Vec models by aligning principal geometry and preserving semantic consistency. It consistently beats prior distillation methods across MMEB tasks and distribution settings.
AI.motivation: Compact VLM2Vec distillation is difficult because teacher and student differ in tokenization, dimensionality, and multimodal capacity.
AI.method: PGA-KD combines Principal Geometry Alignment for stable structural matching with mutual-information maximization for intra- and inter-modal semantic consistency.
AI.result: On all four MMEB meta-tasks under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution conditions, the approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art distillation methods.
AI.conclusion: Jointly preserving geometric structure and semantic dependency mitigates capacity mismatch in multimodal embedding distillation.

title: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments

AI.tldr: AnTrap evaluates Android GUI agents under dynamic runtime anomalies and finds universal vulnerability. Adversarial RL helps with simple traps but not deep contextual failures such as state deadlock.
AI.motivation: GUI agents face pop-ups and action misuse in deployment, but existing benchmarks do not systematically evaluate runtime-anomaly robustness.
AI.method: AnTrap injects solvability-preserving perturbations organized into four layers and ten subcategories, then evaluates 16 GUI models and GRPO training in original and adversarial environments.
AI.result: Even the strongest models degrade substantially; state- and action-layer single-step traps are largely learnable, whereas deep contextual traps remain unresolved by trap-only training.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic anomalies reveal agent limitations that require more than adversarial training on isolated runtime traps.

title: PrimeTTT: Priming Test-Time Training for LLMs via Meta-Learned Initialization

AI.tldr: PrimeTTT uses meta-learned prompt-specific LoRA initialization to improve LLM test-time training. It consistently outperforms strong TTT baselines across unseen benchmarks and model families.
AI.motivation: Vanilla TTT gives limited gains because LLMs are not trained as gradient-adaptation initializations and prompt-masked NTP is misaligned with answer correctness.
AI.method: A hypernetwork produces LoRA initialization; a MAML-style objective backpropagates answer-conditioned NTP through inner-loop PM-NTP updates.
AI.result: Across out-of-distribution benchmarks disjoint from training, PrimeTTT consistently surpasses strong TTT baselines and transfers across model scales and families.
AI.conclusion: Meta-learning adaptation-ready initializations can overcome key optimization and objective-alignment limits of test-time training.

title: Right Answers for the Right Reasons: Coherence-Enhanced Policy Optimization for Large Language Models

AI.tldr: CE-PO improves LLM policy optimization by rewarding coherence between prompt, rationale, and answer alongside task accuracy. It increases both reasoning accuracy and faithful reasoning.
AI.motivation: RL-trained LLMs can obtain correct answers through shortcuts and unfaithful rationales, making them brittle to small input changes.
AI.method: CE-PO estimates Jacobian-based pathway coherence, residualizes shortcut effects through reshuffling, and fuses coherence with accuracy using an Lp reward combiner compatible with PPO and GRPO.
AI.result: Across reasoning benchmarks, CE-PO improves accuracy by 5.49 points on average, up to 9.58, and faithful reasoning by 12.14% on average across five backbones.
AI.conclusion: Coherence-aware reward fusion can encourage right answers for faithful reasons without architectural changes.

title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL

AI.tldr: ContextPilot teaches agents proactive context management with expanded tools and fine-grained RL. It improves long-context QA and deep search while keeping a more compact working context.
AI.motivation: Existing context-management agents have limited tools, inefficiently explore heterogeneous editing actions, and assign one final reward to all edits.
AI.method: ContextPilot adds planning, long-term-memory, and soft-offloading tools, then branches on actions identified by context and entropy variation and estimates action-level advantages from traversing trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments on long-context QA and deep-search tasks show stronger performance and more compact working context than existing baselines across base models and benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Specialized tools and action-level credit assignment enable more effective proactive context control for long-horizon agents.

title: From Agent Skills to Executable Environments: Frontier-Targeted Training for Tool-Use LLMs

AI.tldr: Grafting converts agent skills into validated executable tool-use environments, and Fathoming trains on capability-frontier trajectories. The resulting 4B model makes large out-of-distribution gains on tool-use benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Tool-use LLM training lacks scalable stateful environments and verified multi-turn trajectories matched to a target model's current capability boundary.
AI.method: Grafting has coding-agent harnesses build and refine executable environments under deterministic validation; Fathoming iteratively applies GRPO to verified near-frontier trajectories.
AI.result: Grafting produces 500 environments and about 12K trajectories; Fathom-4B raises BFCLv4 multi-turn accuracy from 22.0 to 39.7 and ComplexFuncBench per-call accuracy from 49.6 to 61.6. The pipeline also creates 5,101-environment Grove-5K.
AI.conclusion: Agent skills can seed scalable verified environments and frontier-targeted trajectories for improving tool-use LLMs.
